sections.content: How many people are "registered mental health nurses"?

28,160 people

were counted on the census as "registered mental health nurses" in England and Wales in March 2021.

Registered mental health nurses support and care for people with a range of mental health conditions, in hospital and community settings, and help them towards recovery and management of their conditions.

People who had this job were generally similar in age to the working population

The occupation of "registered mental health nurses" had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 50 to 54 years. Of the whole working population 11.7% were aged 50 to 54 years. For people working as "registered mental health nurses", 14.1% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "registered mental health nurses" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "registered mental health nurses" included:

  • protective service associate professionals (other)
  • information technology trainers
  • other drivers and transport operatives

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

More women than men had this job

Among people working as "registered mental health nurses" there were more women than men (74.5% compared with 25.5%).

This means "registered mental health nurses" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "health professionals".

Men made up 25.5% and women made up 74.5% of "registered mental health nurses"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "registered mental health nurses" included:

  • probation officers
  • book-keepers, payroll managers and wages clerks
  • education managers

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "registered mental health nurses", 12.6% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (80.2% compared with 19.8%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (95.2%) than self-employed (4.8%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the North West. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Birmingham, this is in the region of the West Midlands.
